v.why: Low learning rates under-train in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps much more than when the rate is already adequate.
Already-large learning rates push Adam toward divergence, so a further increase hurts.
Reducing an excessive learning rate restores stable training.
Very strong L2 penalty collapses the weights, so weakening it recovers accuracy.
Increasing an already strong penalty causes underfitting.
Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, so smaller batches add useful optimization steps.
Going to even larger batches further reduces the number of updates and causes underfitting.
With a low learning rate, fewer updates from larger batches leave the model under-trained.
Deeper networks are more unstable at high learning rates, so adding depth there tends to hurt.
Wider layers speed up learning when the learning rate is small and the model is underfit.

raw:
I'm proposing these from the 100 single-seed experiments plus general reasoning about Adam training for 243 epochs. I ran no new experiments, and the evidence for several of these is thin.

- **Learning rate:** Raising it helps when it starts low (experiments 61, 69) and hurts when it starts high (64, 66). Lowering it from a high value helps (74, 78).
- **Alpha:** An alpha of 1 is heavily over-regularized. Lowering it there gave large gains (20), and raising it from high values tended to hurt (3).
- **Batch size:** Very large batches at low learning rate under-train. Stepping the batch size down helped there (39), and stepping it up hurt (29).
- **Depth:** Adding depth at high learning rates risks instability (44).
- **Width:** Adding width helps when a low learning rate leaves the model underfit (89).
